claims.text: An amorphous metal oxide has a high-surface-area, porous structure.
The amorphous metal oxide provides a suitable platform for surface functionalization.
The proposed intervention is surface functionalization with noble-metal nanoparticles.
Surface functionalization produces surface defects and a beneficial distribution of noble-metal nanoparticles.
The surface defects and nanoparticle distribution create a high-density array of active sites.
These active sites promote hydrogen adsorption and desorption.
The modified surface composition and structure reduce hydrogen binding energy.
The modified surface increases the surface mobility of hydrogen species.
The modification increases hydrogen adsorption capacity by 20%.
The modification decreases the hydrogen desorption energy barrier by 30%.
The surface-functionalized electrocatalyst exhibits enhanced HER and HOR catalytic activity and durability.
The proposed catalyst increases exchange current density by 30% relative to commercial Pt/C.
The proposed catalyst decreases Tafel slope by 25% relative to commercial Pt/C.
A potential range of -1.0 to 1.0 V versus RHE is applicable to the proposed electrochemical operation.
Operation from 20 to 80 °C allows optimal electrocatalytic activity.
Operation from 1 to 5 atm ensures stable and efficient mass transport of reactants and products.
Performance may depend on synthesis method, surface-functionalization protocol, and operating conditions.

contradictions.description: The predicted outcome requires a 30% exchange-current-density increase and a 25% Tafel-slope decrease, but the falsification rule permits substantially weaker performance without falsification: an exchange current density from 1.1 to below 1.3 times baseline and a Tafel slope from 0.75 to 1.1 times baseline would miss the stated prediction but not necessarily trigger the rule.
